target: At least 99 percent of atomic source-to-destination links correct, demonstrated by independent scan-grounded evaluation

baseline.note: Aggregate from existing V2 interpreted shard texts; OCR-derived counts, NOT verified totals; rows may omit/collapse references

questions.question: When a marginal reference has no book prefix, does its destination inherit the source book of the current page (e.g. Genesis here), does it inherit the preceding target book in the margin, or is there a conditional editorial rule?

What does the printed equals sign mean here? Does it change source/destination scope or just indicate a comparison/cross-reference? Should '= 15' be understood as chapter 15, verse 15, or a continuation of an earlier notation?

The visible print 's 14 14+' (D040) and 'Ch 1 1-4' (D042) was already confirmed against scans. What do these abbreviations mean as canonical target books? Is the leading 's' a physically incomplete book abbreviation/continuation, and what exact book is meant by 'Ch' here? No need to reverify the visible characters.

For independent database connections, should 'Si 43 6,7' produce two target edges (Sir 43:6 and Sir 43:7) or a single destination referencing a verse set? Confirm that 'Ps 8; 104' yields two distinct chapter references.

For suffixes +, s, ss and p, should the import preserve exactly the printed suffix on its target coordinate without manufacturing an inferred end verse? Are any of these editorial markers that change the number of distinct destination links?
questions.assumed_rule: Preserve printed suffix as metadata; never synthesize unseen target coordinates

known_issue.lesson: Even correctly exposed print can lose chapter-versus-verse typography; this is not a cropped-edge case.
